findings.summary: crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The root-proof lock is written a second time in athena-core instead of being shared with athena-git.
findings.evidence: athena-git/src/snapshot.rs:161-197 holds `Snapshot::lock` and `probe_write`. Its helpers `set_tree_writable` (399, which handles entries that vanish during the walk) and `set_immutable` (459) are private. Only `unlock_dir` (389) is pub. The plan writes its own `lock` in athena-core so it does not touch a file outside the expected set, which means copying both private helpers. A security primitive would then exist in two copies that can drift apart. Fix: Add a `pub fn lock_dir(dir, existing_probe: &Path)` next to `unlock_dir` in athena-git/src/snapshot.rs, have `Snapshot::lock` call it, and use it from athena-core. If the planner keeps the copy, say why. Touching one more file in athena-git is a smaller risk than having two lock implementations.

findings.summary: Counting jobs by `job.state()` names will not match `athena status` for in-flight jobs or for jobs that are not request jobs.
findings.evidence: status.rs:1680-1696 counts only `records.request_jobs()` and maps names through `state_name`: Dispatched becomes `running` or `interrupted` (1650-1655). The plan says it 'counts `job.state()` names' over the loaded records. The criterion 3 test compares `jobs_by_state` with `athena.status()`, so it passes only on a fixture where every job has landed. Fix: Iterate `records.request_jobs()` the way status does, and give Dispatched one fixed name such as `dispatched`, with a note that a snapshot cannot tell whether the job is running. Add a dispatched-but-not-closed job to the criterion 3 fixture, or document and test the difference.

findings.summary: Writing the tree's and the records-branch tip's landing files into one directory can collide on the same path, and load_dir's file order is not specified.
findings.evidence: store.rs:377-382 keeps both sources, then sorts by (created_at, id) and dedups by id. A flat copy that writes tip files over tree files with the same relative path can drop one version before that dedup runs. Several `Records` fields are kept 'in file order' (store.rs:229-236). `RecordSet::load` uses git's recursive tree order (athena-gate/src/records.rs:27-55), while a directory walk returns entries in no fixed order. Fix: State the collision rule: keep the tree's file and skip a tip file with the same path, or write the tip's files under a separate subdirectory that `load_dir` also reads. Have `load_dir` sort full relative paths bytewise, which reproduces git's recursive order.

findings.summary: If the host rejects `--add-dir` under `--restricted`, every producer and verifier run fails, and nothing in `cargo test` would catch it.
findings.evidence: claude.rs `command_line` (114-148) gains the flag for producer and verifier whenever the evidence directory exists, which after this change is every dispatch. The only real-host test, athena-cli/tests/live.rs, is `#[ignore]`d. The plan's mitigation covers the host ignoring the flag, not rejecting it. Fix: Keep the Host open question. Also either (a) say the ignored live test must be run once against the pinned host before landing, or (b) add a fallback: if an invocation fails with an unknown-option error mentioning `--add-dir`, retry once without the flag (the hook still enforces the policy). Name which one.

findings.summary: The system-facts entry 'Producer snapshot' stays literally true but no longer tells planners that an evidence snapshot exists.
findings.evidence: The system facts say producers have no `records/` or history, with the producer brief text as the source. After this change producers and verifiers can read `<state>/jobs/<id>/evidence`. Planners read this file to design real-records demonstrations, and Decision 8 keeps the evidence path out of the planner brief. Fix: Add one sentence to the system-facts entry (outside the budgeted sets) naming the evidence snapshot and `athena status --snapshot`, or list it as a named follow-up.
findings.location: Dependents: 'Prompt-set budgets and the Producer snapshot fact'

findings.summary: Building the sent prompt by string replacement is less direct than rendering the brief twice.
findings.evidence: `producer_brief_with_evidence` is a pure function. Calling it once with `Some(placeholder)` for the stored brief and once with `Some(real)` for the prompt avoids rewriting user text that happens to contain the placeholder. The verifier side already does it this way (step 8). Fix: Call `producer_brief_with_evidence` twice, the same way as the verifier.

findings.summary: `read_dirs` is a host argument, not part of how the hook reaches the policy.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-agent/src/lib.rs:42-49 documents HookSpec as 'How the hook reaches Athena's tool policy'. Fix: Keep it there if moving it would touch many `AgentInvocation` literals, but update the HookSpec doc comment to say it also carries the extra read-only directories passed to the host.

summary: I read the code the plan names and found its claims true. `Records::load` (store.rs:311) is the only place records are assembled, and `Throughput::compute` (status.rs:929) reads only `Records`, so sharing `from_parts` gives identical throughput text without touching the computation. `Snapshot::lock` and `unlock_dir` (athena-git snapshot.rs:161, 389), `pin::remove_tree` (pin.rs:221) and `clean_job` (state.rs:333) work as the plan says, so a locked evidence directory is cleaned up. In dispatch (run/mod.rs:837-979) the disk gates run before the brief is built and the brief is committed verbatim, so storing a placeholder and sending the real path is correct. `brief_sha256` is never recomputed. The `Policy` and `HookSpec` literals listed are all of them (I grepped). `Policy` uses `deny_unknown_fields`, so a defaulted field still accepts old files, including the one binary.rs writes. Verifiers may run `cargo run` (athena.toml:76), so `athena status --snapshot` is reachable, and cargo arguments are not path-confined (policy.rs:623-652). The planner-side check `plan_findings` simulates a verifier policy rooted at the job directory, which already contains `evidence`, so `evidence: None` in planning.rs is harmless. Each demonstration names a real seam: `athena_with` (run/tests.rs:183), `producer_inputs` and `plain_verifier_inputs`, and the binary. Each would fail without the behavior, and the read-only test shows a write succeeding before the lock and failing after it, as root. Athena's own finding about refusal_corpus.rs is unavoidable: those two literals must compile. My findings are minor. The lock logic is copied instead of shared. The snapshot's jobs-by-state does not match `athena status`. The merged landings copy can collide and its file order is unspecified. A host that rejects `--add-dir` would break every run. The system-facts entry is now incomplete. None blocks the plan.
